en: And al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Hulwani and Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to us—both saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Halhalah informed me, from Wahb ibn Kaysan, from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, that he said: I ate one day with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and I began taking from the meat around the dish. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Eat from what is nearest to you."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, both from Sufyan—Abu Bakr said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn Kathir, from Wahb ibn Kaysan, who heard it from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, who said: I was a boy in the lap of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and my hand would wander around the dish. So he said to me: "O young boy, mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is nearest to you."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, from Ikrimah ibn Ammar: Iyas ibn Salamah ibn al-Akwa' narrated to me, that his father narrated to him, that a man was eating in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with his left hand. So he said: "Eat with your right hand." The man said: "I cannot." He said: "May you not be able!" Nothing prevented him except pride. He said: And he never raised it to his mouth again.

And Abu at-Tahir and Harmalah narrated to me—Abu at-Tahir said "informed us" and Harmalah said "narrated to us"—: Abdallah ibn Wahb narrated to us: Umar ibn Muhammad narrated to me: al-Qasim ibn Ubaydillah ibn Abdillah ibn Umar narrated to him, from Salim, from his father: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should eat with his left hand, nor drink with it, for Satan eats with his left hand and drinks with it." He said: And Nafi' used to add to it: "nor take with it, nor give with it." And in the narration of Abu at-Tahir: "None of you should eat."

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas in what was read to him (H); and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us (H); and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya—and he is al-Qattan—narrated to us, both from Ubaydullah, all of them from az-Zuhri, with the chain of narration of Sufyan.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn Numayr's—they said: Sufyan narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Ubaydillah ibn Abdillah ibn Umar, from his grandfather Ibn Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When one of you eats, let him eat with his right hand; and when he drinks, let him drink with his right hand, for Satan eats with his left hand and drinks with his left hand."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us (H); and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Do not eat with the left hand, for Satan eats with the left hand."

And Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated it to me: Rawh ibn Ubadah informed us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Abu az-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying that he heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying... a narration similar to the hadith of Abu Asim, except that he said: "and if he does not mention the name of Allah at his meal, and if he does not mention the name of Allah upon his entering."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Anazi narrated to us: ad-Dahhak—meaning Abu Asim—narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj: Abu az-Zubayr informed me, from Jabir ibn Abdillah, that he heard the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "When a man enters his home and mentions Allah upon entering and upon eating, Satan says: 'You have no lodging and no dinner.' But when he enters and does not mention Allah upon entering, Satan says: 'You have found lodging.' And when he does not mention Allah upon eating, he says: 'You have found lodging and dinner.'"

And Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' narrated it to me: Abd ar-Rahman narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, with this chain of narration, and he placed the arrival of the girl before the arrival of the Bedouin.

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated it to us: Isa ibn Yunus informed us: al-A'mash informed us, from Khaythamah ibn Abd ar-Rahman, from Abu Hudhayfah al-Arhabi, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who said: Whenever we were invited with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to a meal... and he mentioned the hadith with the meaning of the narration of Abu Mu'awiyah, and said: "as if he were being pushed", and regarding the girl: "as if she were being pushed", and he placed the arrival of the Bedouin in his hadith before the arrival of the girl, and added at the end of the hadith: "Then he mentioned the name of Allah and ate."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—both saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Khaythamah, from Abu Hudhayfah, from Hudhayfah, who said: When we attended a meal with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), we would not put our hands to it until the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) started and put his hand. And once we attended a meal with him, when a young girl came rushing as if she were being pushed, and went to put her hand into the food, but the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) took her hand. Then a Bedouin came rushing as if he were being pushed, and he took his hand. Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Satan considers food lawful to himself when Allah's name is not mentioned over it; and he brought this girl so that he might make it lawful through her, but I took her hand; then he brought this Bedouin so that he might make it lawful through him, but I took his hand. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, Satan's hand is in my hand along with her hand!"

Sa'id ibn Amr al-Ash'athi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr, Abu Amir al-Ash'ari, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Amir's—they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: A house burned down over its inhabitants in Medina at night. When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was informed of their matter, he said: "Indeed, this fire is an enemy to you; so when you sleep, extinguish it."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr an-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—they said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from az-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Do not leave fire burning in your houses when you sleep."

And Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdhami narrated to us: my father narrated to me: Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, with this chain of narration, a similar narration, except that he said: "For indeed, there is a day in the year when an epidemic descends." And he added at the end of the hadith: al-Layth said: "The non-Arabs among us beware of that in Kanun al-Awwal (December)."

And Amr an-Naqid narrated to us: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us: al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us: Yazid ibn Abdillah ibn Usamah ibn al-Had al-Laythi narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Ja'far ibn Abdillah ibn al-Hakam, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Jabir ibn Abdillah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Cover the vessels and tie up the water skins, for indeed there is a night in the year when an epidemic descends; it does not pass by any vessel without a cover or water skin without a tie but some of that epidemic descends into it."

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Abd ar-Rahman narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a narration similar to the hadith of Zuhayr.

And Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu az-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir (H); and Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not send out your wandering cattle and your children when the sun has set until the darkness of early night has passed, for the devils are let loose when the sun has set until the darkness of early night has passed."
And Ahmad ibn Uthman an-Nawfali narrated to us: Abu Asim narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us with this hadith, from Ata' and Amr ibn Dinar, like the narration of Rawh.

And Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Rawh ibn Ubadah informed us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Amr ibn Dinar informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying similar to what Ata' reported, except that he did not say: "Mention the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

And Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me: Rawh ibn Ubadah informed us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Ata' informed us that he heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When the wings of night fall—or when evening comes—keep your children in, for the devils spread out at that time; and when an hour of the night has passed, let them go; and close the doors and mention the name of Allah, for Satan does not open a closed door; and tie up your water skins and mention the name of Allah; and cover your vessels and mention the name of Allah, even if you only place something across them; and extinguish your lamps."

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Abd ar-Rahman narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a narration similar to their hadith, and he said: "and the little noxious creature (mouse) sets fire to the house upon its inhabitants."

And Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu az-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Close the door..." and he mentioned a narration similar to the hadith of al-Layth, except that he said: "and cover the vessels," and he said: "sets fire to the clothes of the inhabitants of the house."

And Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with this hadith, except that he said: "and turn the vessel upside down or cover the vessel," and he did not mention placing a stick across the vessel.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us (H); and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "Cover the vessel, tie up the water skin, close the door, and extinguish the lamp; for indeed Satan does not untie a water skin, nor does he open a door, nor does he uncover a vessel. If one of you finds nothing except to place a stick across his vessel and mention the name of Allah, let him do so; for indeed the little noxious creature sets fire to the house upon its inhabitants." And Qutaybah did not mention in his hadith: "and close the door."

And Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan and Abu Salih, from Jabir, who said: A man called Abu Humayd came with a cup of milk from an-Naqi', and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "Why did you not cover it, even if you were only to place a stick across it?"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Kurayb's—both saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Jabir ibn Abdillah, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and he asked for a drink. A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not give you nabidh to drink?" He said: "Yes." He said: So the man went running and brought a cup containing nabidh, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Why did you not cover it, even if you were only to place a stick across it?" He said: Then he drank.

And Ibrahim ibn Dinar narrated to me: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj and Zakariyya ibn Ishaq narrated to us—both saying: Abu az-Zubayr informed us that he heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: Abu Humayd as-Sa'idi informed me that he came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with a cup of milk... a similar narration. He said: And Zakariyya did not mention the statement of Abu Humayd: "at night."

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—all from Abu Asim; Ibn al-Muthanna said: ad-Dahhak narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Abu az-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: Abu Humayd as-Sa'idi informed me, saying: I came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with a cup of milk from an-Naqi' that was uncovered, so he said: "Why did you not cover it, even if you were only to place a stick across it?" Abu Humayd said: "The command was only that water skins be tied at night and that doors be closed at night."

And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us (H); and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us: an-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, both from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: Abu Bakr bought a saddle from my father for thirteen dirhams... and he related the hadith with the meaning of the hadith of Zuhayr from Abu Ishaq. And he said in his hadith from the narration of Uthman ibn Umar: When he drew near, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) supplicated against him, so his horse sank into the ground up to its belly. He jumped off it and said: "O Muhammad, I have known that this is your doing; so pray to Allah to save me from what I am in, and I promise you that I will divert anyone behind me away from you. And here is my quiver; take an arrow from it, for you will pass by my camels and my servants in such-and-such place, so take from them whatever you need." He said: "I have no need of your camels." Then we arrived in Medina at night, and they disputed as to which of them the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would stay with. He said: "I will stay with Banu an-Najjar, the maternal uncles of Abd al-Muttalib, honoring them by that." Then men and women climbed atop the houses, and young boys and servants dispersed throughout the streets calling out: "O Muhammad! O Messenger of Allah! O Muhammad! O Messenger of Allah!"
